candidates.description: The system should provide a user-friendly query-design interface for bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, and financial records, allowing users to select query fields, choose values from picklists, select regular expressions from a drop-down menu, and use Boolean operators, while administrators control staff access to tables and fields.

candidates.name: Executive Report Suite
candidates.description: The system should provide predefined reports for library boards and other external consumers, including basic statistics required by the Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid.

candidates.name: Activity Cross-Tabulation
candidates.description: Activity reports should show traffic and usage volumes for check-outs, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled, with cross-tabulation by terminal, branch, library system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location.

candidates.name: Privacy-Preserving Archives
candidates.description: The system must archive transactions in a form that protects patron privacy as defined by State Law while retaining useful demographic statistics.

candidates.name: Periodic Management Reports
candidates.description: The system should provide periodic reports for bibliographic records with holds; items not checked out in a configurable number of days; item-level holds; invalid item types; in-transit items with outstanding holds; items in transit beyond a configurable number of days; last copies; long call numbers; missing items; bibliographic records without item records; and patrons with invalid home libraries.

candidates.name: Query Criteria Display
candidates.description: The system should display the query selections or criteria together with report results so users can see which criteria generated the report.

candidates.name: Report Queue Visibility
candidates.description: Staff should be able to see the position of their report in the queue of reports waiting to run.

candidates.name: Patron Behavior Statistics
candidates.description: The system should produce statistics for understanding and predicting patron behavior and material use, including average return speed for a particular book, likelihood of renewal, and the percentage of check-outs at a branch that are renewals.

candidates.name: Anonymized Demographic Statistics
candidates.description: The system should produce demographic statistics such as transactions by geographic region and age range using anonymized data from which information that could identify a patron has been deleted.

candidates.name: Material Volume Reporting
candidates.description: The system must report the volume of material in a library at any point in time based on new acquisitions, shelf items, and items in circulation, with breakdowns such as total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books.

candidates.name: Branch Capacity Interface
candidates.description: The system should provide an interface showing the capacity of all branches.

candidates.name: Shelf Space Comparison
candidates.description: The system must compare, for each material genre and format and per library or system, the percentage of total circulations, percentage of the collection, and percentage of total shelf space.

candidates.name: Uncataloged Material Control
candidates.description: The system must control inventory of uncataloged materials such as paperback books and children's board books, supporting quick distribution, minimal branch labor, identification of material use, and counting these transactions in circulation statistics and reports.

candidates.name: Batch Item Transfers
candidates.description: The system must provide a utility for transferring batches of items between branches, including querying and saving candidate-material queries, manually selecting titles from results, changing selected item records to a new location, moving items by changing location fields or generating pull lists, and reverting items to their original location after a set period.

candidates.name: Missing Damaged Reports
candidates.description: The system should provide missing-item and damaged-item reports by branch.

candidates.name: In-Transit Reporting
candidates.description: The system should generate a merged report of items in transit for more than a configurable number of days, organized per branch and per system and combining transit-to and transit-from information for front-line staff.

candidates.name: Item Purge Management
candidates.description: The system must provide utilities and reports to identify item records for purging using customizable criteria, including items missing longer than a configurable number of months and items with discard or weed status; it must also support status-conversion reports, last-copy reports, deletion of volume entries with copy entries, and handling records with no attached items.

candidates.name: Deletion Tracking
candidates.description: The system must count and track deleted records, including item and patron records, by location and by system.

candidates.name: Patron Characteristic Filtering
candidates.description: Queries and reports must be limitable or groupable by patron age range, zip code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, and preferred language.

candidates.name: Inactive Patron Reporting
candidates.description: The system should generate a configurable report of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity during the previous configurable number of days, filterable or organized by system, home library, county, and similar organizational scope.

candidates.name: Transaction History Retention
candidates.description: The system must retain detailed transaction history for a configurable number of days and retain monthly and annual aggregate information indefinitely.

candidates.name: Transaction Grouping
candidates.description: The system must group transactions by hour, terminal, branch, and system and support querying all transactions or transaction types, including check-ins, check-outs, fines collected, and patron registrations.

candidates.name: Check-In Type Counts
candidates.description: The system must count check-ins both individually and cumulatively by book drop, terminal, and user or self-service source.

candidates.name: Check-Out Type Counts
candidates.description: The system must count check-outs both individually and cumulatively by staff check-out, self check-out, staff renewal, self-checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal.

candidates.name: Hold Placement Counts
candidates.description: The system must count all hold requests and record how each hold was placed, including at a staff desk, at a public computer inside the library, or remotely.

candidates.name: Transaction Summary Reports
candidates.description: The system must generate transaction reports for holds placed, holds filled, and check-outs per patron, library, selected group of libraries, system, or county; display check-outs and placed holds per patron; and subtotal holds by types such as active, frozen, and frozen-until.

candidates.name: Collection Value Reporting
candidates.description: The system must report item values, based on item-record data, for the entire collection or a portion of it, including items selected by status, format, collection, or other report criteria.

candidates.name: Accounting Audit Compliance
candidates.description: All reports and archived data must comply with standard accounting practice and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.

candidates.name: Patron Financial Records
candidates.description: The system must attach fines, charges, waivers, and ecommerce transactions to patron and item records, track fines waived and payments made per library, support easy financial-information updates, and allow queries such as patron accounts with balances above a specified dollar threshold.

candidates.name: Financial Report Suite
candidates.description: The system must provide reports of patron account balances by patron, home library, and system; fines and charges by time period and charge type; fines waived by time period and branch; and payments by time period and payment method, including staff desk, self-check station, and OPAC.

candidates.name: Payment Audit Ledger
candidates.description: The system must maintain a ledger of patron payments identifying the charges to which payments were applied, to support reconciliation.

candidates.name: Circulation Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support circulation reports for check-in count; checkout count; items overdue by a specified number of days with daily, shelf-reading, and patron-contact information; circulation by circulation modifier, category, Dewey classification, shelving location, MARC data, patron county, patron home library, and age demographic; renewals; non-cataloged circulation; total circulation including checkouts, renewals, and non-cataloged circulation; and merged cataloged and non-cataloged circulation.

candidates.name: Item Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support item reports for items added, deleted, edited, counted, currently checked out, overdue beyond a specified number of days, marked long overdue, above or below a total-use threshold, created within a date range, missing, in transit by sending and destination libraries, claimed returned, long overdue, containing specified bibliographic text, and items to be converted; reports must also cover fines-stopped reasons, last copies deleted by a library system, weeding data with last-circulation date and circulation count, collection age by call number or shelving location, collection price value by call number or shelving location, and items with specified total use.

candidates.name: Bibliographic Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support reports for bibliographic-record counts, edited-record counts, records added by user and library, records with no attached volumes, and records missing specified MARC fields.

candidates.name: Patron Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support reports for patron counts; patrons added by month; new patrons by demographic category; patrons by age, county, home library, profile group, survey answer, expiration date, inactive status, note wording, and barred status; survey-answer patron lists; voter survey responses by county and week; voter-registration survey response counts by week; and staff accounts showing last password change and account expiration.

candidates.name: Hold Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support reports for hold purchase alerts; items sent or received for holds; IntraPINES loans for all systems, facilities, systems, and facilities; unfilled holds; annual hold counts; and stale holds waiting on hold shelves beyond the permitted pickup period.

candidates.name: In-House Use Reports
candidates.description: The system must support reports for non-cataloged in-house use counts by month and cataloged in-house use counts.

candidates.name: Transit Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support reports for items in transit to a destination library and items in transit by sending library.

candidates.name: Bills Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support reports for bills currently owed by patrons, detailed payments received, detailed forgive/work/goods payments received, detailed voids, and aged debt.

candidates.name: Canned Report Interface
candidates.description: The system must provide a canned-report interface for generic reports that individuals can run immediately or on a recurring schedule.

candidates.name: On-Demand Report Interface
candidates.description: The system must provide an on-demand report interface for preset maintenance, collection-development, and similar reports whose selection criteria and display options can be edited before execution.

candidates.name: Open Template Reporting
candidates.description: The system must provide open-template reporting with circulation, item, patron, bill, and bibliographic attributes available for both filtering and display.

candidates.name: Scheduled Report Access
candidates.description: The quick-access reporting interface must allow users to view descriptions by hovering over canned report or template titles, select portions of data, and schedule reports ASAP, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.

candidates.name: Report Export Formats
candidates.description: Reports must be exportable in Excel, HTML, and CSV formats.

candidates.name: Report Email Delivery
candidates.description: The system must allow users to enter email addresses for report delivery and should provide an address book for regularly used addresses.

candidates.name: Recurring Report Editing
candidates.description: Users must be able to edit recurring reports by adding or removing report selections and changing their email addresses.

candidates.name: Comparative Report Columns
candidates.description: The system must support report outputs with comparative columns such as last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, percentage difference, the corresponding month of the previous year, and percentage difference between the prior month and prior year's month.

candidates.name: Canned Report Extension
candidates.description: Authorized users must be able to add more canned reports according to permission level and edit canned-report display fields, such as adding shelving location.

candidates.name: Report Queue Prioritization
candidates.description: The system must allow certain report types to be prioritized above resource-consuming reports in the execution queue.

candidates.name: Item Usage Reporting
candidates.description: The system must provide total item-use counts and usage counts broken down by date ranges such as fiscal year or month.

candidates.name: Detailed Circulation Totals
candidates.description: The system must retrieve total circulation including checkouts, renewals, and non-cataloged circulation and display a breakdown by circulation type.

candidates.name: File-Based Report Filtering
candidates.description: Users must be able to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values to filter a report.

candidates.name: Notice Activity Reports
candidates.description: The system must support reports on pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices sent.

candidates.name: Pivot Table Output
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide pivot-table output.

candidates.name: Report Output Validation
candidates.description: Report output must be tested and proven accurate for its intended reporting purpose.

candidates.name: Report Cancellation
candidates.description: Users must be able to cancel a report that is scheduled to run or is currently running.

candidates.name: Include Null Fields
candidates.description: Report results must include all null and blank fields regardless of the selected filtering or display criteria.

candidates.name: Real-Time Reporting
candidates.description: The system must support real-time reporting.

candidates.name: Historical Reporting Warehouse
candidates.description: The system must support historical reporting through a reporting warehouse that can provide data for a specified date or date range.

candidates.name: Explicit Selection Criteria
candidates.description: The reporting interface must clearly define the selection criteria used for a report.

candidates.name: Report Date Metadata
candidates.description: Report results must display the selected date criteria and report name at the top or bottom of the results.

candidates.name: Survey Name Filtering
candidates.description: Users must be able to select a survey by survey name rather than entering its survey ID when filtering reports.

candidates.name: Last-Copy Deletion Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide reports identifying deleted items that were the last copy owned by a library system or facility, supporting WorldCat updates.

candidates.name: Single-Row MARC Fields
candidates.description: The system must be able to extract MARC record fields so that they appear on a single row of report data.

candidates.name: Workstation Transaction Reports
candidates.description: The system must support reports for transactions occurring on a specified date and time, workstation, or staff member.

candidates.name: Generate Item Value Reports
candidates.description: The system must generate reports showing the value of items based on item-record data, including the purchase price, for the entire collection or a selected portion such as all items with status "longoverdue" or all DVDs in the children's collection.

candidates.name: Report Patron Account Balances
candidates.description: The system must provide financial reports of patron account balances by individual patron, home library, and the overall system.

candidates.name: Report Accrued Fines Charges
candidates.description: The system must provide reports of fines and charges accrued during selectable time periods, including the last 12 months, year to date, and last month, and by charge type such as overdue fines, damaged-item charges, and lost-item charges.

candidates.name: Report Waived Fines
candidates.description: The system must provide reports of fines waived by selectable time period and by branch or library, so each library can track waivers against its own budget.

candidates.name: Report Payment Transactions
candidates.description: The system must provide reports of payments made during selectable time periods and by payment method, including staff desk, self-check station, OPAC, cash, credit card, and check, with payments also tracked by the library where they were collected.

candidates.name: Query High-Balance Accounts
candidates.description: The system must allow staff to query patron accounts whose balances are greater than a user-specified dollar amount, so accounts needing attention can be identified efficiently.

candidates.name: Join Financial Data Sources
candidates.description: The system must support financial-report queries that join financial data attached to patron records with financial data attached to item records.

candidates.name: Update Financial Information Immediately
candidates.description: The system must allow financial information to be updated easily and must reflect a patron payment at the front desk immediately in the relevant financial records.

candidates.name: Maintain Payment Audit Ledger
candidates.description: The system must maintain a ledger of patron payments that identifies the specific charges to which each payment was applied, enabling finance staff to trace payments and reconcile accounts.
candidates.source_priority_note: D11 identifies the financial audit trail as CRITICAL

candidates.name: Meet Financial Compliance Requirements
candidates.description: The system's financial reports and data archiving must comply with standard accounting practice and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.

candidates.name: Enforce Data Retention Policies
candidates.description: The system must enforce data-archiving retention policies, including retaining data required for audit purposes for seven years where applicable under state and local requirements.

candidates.name: Design Queries Across Records
candidates.description: The system must provide a user-friendly query-design interface that works against all record types and lets staff select query fields, choose values from picklists, select regular expressions from a dropdown, and use Boolean operators.

candidates.name: Manage Report Templates
candidates.description: The system must let administrators create report templates that are available to staff, can be run as-is or modified, and preserve consistent results when modified. Administrators must be able to restrict which filters and display fields staff may alter, such as allowing a call-number range or display-field changes while preventing display of deleted items.

candidates.name: Clone Report Templates
candidates.description: The system must let authorized users clone an existing report or template to create a separate new report variant rather than modifying the original template.

candidates.name: Authorize Report Creation
candidates.description: The system must provide distinct, fine-grained permissions that control which users may create and clone reports.

candidates.name: Control Shared Report Access
candidates.description: The system must let administrators create shared folders that allow or disallow staff from running specific reports and from running ad hoc reports against specific sets of data.

candidates.name: Synchronize Role Permissions
candidates.description: The system must administer report permissions through roles so that changing a user's role, such as from Staff to Manager, automatically updates that user's report permissions.

candidates.name: Provide Board Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide predefined reports for library boards containing basic statistics required for the Georgia Annual Report and activity measures for traffic and usage, including checkouts, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled. The reports must support cross-tabulation by terminal, branch, system, hour, age range, patron type, and patron location.

candidates.name: Archive Private Transactions
candidates.description: The system must retain transaction data for the period required by State law, identified as X years, while protecting patron privacy by excluding personally identifiable information and still providing useful demographic statistics.
candidates.source_priority_note: D12 states that State law requires this transaction retention and privacy protection for compliance

candidates.name: Show Query Selections
candidates.description: The system must provide the query selections or criteria together with the corresponding query results.

candidates.name: Display Report Queue Status
candidates.description: The system must show staff whether their submitted report is in the queue, how many reports are ahead of it, when it was submitted, and its status as waiting, running, completed, or failed.

candidates.name: Prioritize Reports
candidates.description: The system must allow designated important reports, such as a director's board report, to be prioritized so they can move ahead of lower-priority staff ad hoc queries in the report queue.
candidates.source_priority_note: D12 describes report prioritization as crucial and states that important reports should be able to jump the queue

candidates.name: Support Dual Staff Login
candidates.description: The system must support staff authentication through either an optional streamlined method, such as swiping an employee ID badge, or traditional individual username-and-password login. The streamlined method must be available but must not be required, so branches without card-reader infrastructure can continue using traditional login, and using a card must not bypass individual authentication.

candidates.name: Track Logged-In Staff
candidates.description: The system must identify and track which individual staff member is logged in, regardless of whether authentication uses a card swipe or username and password, so staff activity can be audited.

candidates.name: Control Access By Roles
candidates.description: The system must control user rights and privileges through assigned security groups or roles for individual staff members, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups. It must support role-based access such as front desk staff having access to basic reports with limited filters, department heads being able to create and modify templates, and system administrators having full access to reports and permissions.

candidates.name: Administer Security Roles
candidates.description: Administrators must be able to create and manage security groups and roles and assign them to staff members. Changing a staff member's permissions must be achievable by changing the person's role assignment rather than modifying individual permissions.

candidates.name: Circulation By Modifier
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide circulation counts grouped by circulation modifier.

candidates.name: Circulation By Dewey
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide circulation counts grouped by Dewey classification.

candidates.name: Circulation By MARC
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide circulation counts grouped by specified MARC fields.

candidates.name: Circulation By County
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide circulation counts broken down by circulation location and patron county.

candidates.name: Circulation By Age
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide circulation counts grouped by patron age demographic.

candidates.name: Items Edited Count
candidates.description: The reporting system must report the count of items edited.

candidates.name: Fines Stopped Items
candidates.description: The reporting system must list items grouped or filtered by the reason fines were stopped.

candidates.name: Overdue Contact Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must list items overdue by a configurable number of days together with the associated patron contact information.

candidates.name: Items By Total Use
candidates.description: The reporting system must list items having a specified total use count.

candidates.name: Last Copy Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide an enhanced last-copy report identifying items that are the last copy of a title or relevant collection unit.

candidates.name: Items By Creation Date
candidates.description: The reporting system must list items within a specified creation-date range.

candidates.name: Claims Returned Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a report of items or transactions marked claims returned.

candidates.name: Weeding Circulation Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a weeding report that includes each item's date of last circulation.

candidates.name: Collection Age By Call Number
candidates.description: The reporting system must report the age of the collection grouped by call number.

candidates.name: Collection Value By Call
candidates.description: The reporting system must report the price value of the collection grouped by call number.

candidates.name: Bib Records Edited Count
candidates.description: The reporting system must report the count of bibliographic records edited.

candidates.name: Bib Records By Editor
candidates.description: The reporting system must report counts of bibliographic records added by user and by library.

candidates.name: Bib Records Missing MARC
candidates.description: The reporting system must identify bibliographic records missing specified MARC fields.

candidates.name: Patrons By Age
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide patron counts grouped by age demographic.

candidates.name: Patrons By County
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide patron counts grouped by county.

candidates.name: Patrons By Address
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide patron counts grouped by county, city, and ZIP code.

candidates.name: Voter Survey Responses
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a report of voter survey responses.

candidates.name: Inactive Patron List
candidates.description: The reporting system must list patrons with inactive status.

candidates.name: Password Change Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must report staff accounts together with the date of each account's last password change.

candidates.name: Holds Purchase Alert
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a holds purchase alert report.

candidates.name: Unfilled Holds Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must report unfilled holds.

candidates.name: Stale Holds Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must report stale holds.

candidates.name: Detailed Aged Debt
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide an enhanced aged-debt report with detailed debt information.

candidates.name: Report Queue Visibility
candidates.description: The reporting system must show staff the queue position and status of their reports, including reports awaiting processing and reports running in the background.

candidates.name: Report Prioritization
candidates.description: The reporting system must allow authorized users to prioritize selected types of reports.

candidates.name: Cancel Running Reports
candidates.description: The reporting system must allow authorized users to cancel a report that is running.

candidates.name: Pivot Table Output
candidates.description: The reporting system must generate report results in pivot-table format.

candidates.name: Real-Time Reporting
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide reports using current data in real time rather than only through non-real-time report execution.

candidates.name: Historical Reporting Warehouse
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a historical reporting warehouse that supports reporting on data from prior periods.

candidates.name: Report Scheduling Modes
candidates.description: The reporting system must support report execution choices of Run ASAP, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly, including the ability to select multiple reports to run at the same time.

candidates.name: Report Email Delivery
candidates.description: The reporting system must deliver generated reports by email.

candidates.name: Report Delivery Address Book
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide an address book for selecting report delivery recipients.

candidates.name: Text File Filtering
candidates.description: The reporting system must allow users to upload text files containing values such as barcodes or TCNs for use as report filtering criteria.

candidates.name: Selection Criteria Results
candidates.description: The reporting system must display the selection criteria used to produce report results.

candidates.name: Canned Report Options
candidates.description: The reporting system must allow users to edit the display options of canned reports.

candidates.name: Quick Report Access
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a quick-access interface for reports with pop-up descriptions.

candidates.name: Report Title Tooltips
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide hover tooltips for report titles.

candidates.name: Reporting Database Replica
candidates.description: The reporting system must use a separate reporting database or replica so reporting operations are separated from the production database.

candidates.name: Background Report Processing
candidates.description: The reporting system must process long-running reports in the background without requiring them to run interactively against the production operations.

candidates.name: Report Template Management
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide management of report templates, including creating, maintaining, and reusing report definitions.

candidates.name: Fine-Grained Report Permissions
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide fine-grained permissions controlling who can create and run reports, which reports staff can access, and which filters they can use.

candidates.name: Environment Separation
candidates.description: The product must provide separate development and training environments for the reporting system.

candidates.name: Configuration Migration
candidates.description: The reporting system must support migration of configuration between environments.

candidates.name: Accessible Report Interface
candidates.description: The reporting interface must support accessibility compliance.

candidates.name: Integrated Report Help
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide an online help system integrated with the report interface.

candidates.name: On-Demand Reporting Interface
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide an on-demand reporting interface in addition to canned reports.

candidates.name: Open Template Reporting
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide an open-template reporting interface that allows staff to create reports from report templates beyond the basic canned-report interface.

candidates.name: Historical Bills Snapshot
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a bills report that can show a snapshot of bills as they existed at a prior point in time.

candidates.name: Distinct Last Edit Date
candidates.description: The reporting system must report the last edit date for a record without treating the last circulation event as the record's last edit.

candidates.name: Last Circulation Date
candidates.description: The reporting system must expose the date of last circulation as a separate reportable field.

candidates.name: Checkin Date Excluding Renewals
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide check-in date and time separately from renewal timestamps, without combining check-ins and renewals into one timestamp field.

candidates.name: Include Null And Blank Fields
candidates.description: The reporting system must include records whose selected report fields are null or blank in report results rather than filtering them out.

candidates.name: Track Uncataloged Inventory
candidates.description: The system must track shipments of paperback books, children's board books, and other material as inventory before individual catalog records are complete, while supporting rapid distribution with minimal branch labor.

candidates.name: Measure Uncataloged Material Use
candidates.description: The system must identify how uncataloged material is being used and include transactions for that material in circulation statistics and reports.

candidates.name: Query Transfer Candidates
candidates.description: The item transfer utility must query for candidate materials, such as children's-section items that have not circulated in six months, for possible movement between branches or collections.

candidates.name: Save Transfer Queries
candidates.description: The item transfer utility must save candidate-material queries for repeated use, including monthly transfer workflows.

candidates.name: Select Transfer Items
candidates.description: The item transfer utility must allow staff to manually select individual titles from query results when a more targeted transfer is needed.

candidates.name: Change Item Locations
candidates.description: The item transfer utility must change the location records of selected items when they are moved to another branch, mobile library unit, outreach program collection, or other destination.

candidates.name: Revert Item Locations
candidates.description: The item transfer utility must provide a mechanism to return transferred items to their original locations after a defined period, such as when a mobile library returns to its base.

candidates.name: Report Missing Damaged Items
candidates.description: The system must provide a report showing all missing and damaged items by branch to support collection-health monitoring and identification of recurring location patterns.

candidates.name: Report Delayed Transit Items
candidates.description: The system must provide one in-transit-items report that combines transit-to and transit-from items, identifies items in transit longer than a configurable number of days, and supports reporting by branch and by the entire system.

candidates.name: Identify Purge Candidates
candidates.description: The system must provide weeding reports that identify items for purging using customizable criteria, including items in status "missing" for more than a specified number of months and items with status "discard/weed".

candidates.name: Batch Change Item Status
candidates.description: The system must support batch conversion of selected items from one status to another, including changing 100 items from "missing" to "discard/weed".

candidates.name: Report Last Copies
candidates.description: The system must provide a report identifying each library system's last copies so catalogers can check those copies before editing related WorldCat entries or otherwise risking deletion of a rare or unique copy.
candidates.source_priority_note: D15 describes the last copy report as critical

candidates.name: Delete Orphaned Catalog Records
candidates.description: The system must provide a quick method to delete volume entries together with their copy entries and to delete records that have no items attached, supporting cleanup of orphaned catalog records.

candidates.name: Track Record Deletions
candidates.description: The system must count and track record deletions by location and by library system, including why each deletion occurred, so directors can audit deletions and staff can troubleshoot missing catalog content.

candidates.name: Report Shelf Space Allocation
candidates.description: The system must provide a shelf-space report that compares, for each genre and format, the percentage of total circulations, percentage of the collection, and percentage of total shelf space to support resource-allocation decisions.

candidates.name: Report Material Volumes
candidates.description: The system must provide a material-volume report covering acquisitions, items on shelf, and items in circulation, broken down by categories such as total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books.

candidates.name: Report Data Quality Issues
candidates.description: The system must provide data-quality reports identifying items with invalid item types, items with excessively long call numbers, and bibliographic records with no item records.

candidates.name: Display Item Edit Dates
candidates.description: Reports must display the last edit date for an item based on item edits only; the displayed date must not be updated by or include the item's last circulation.

candidates.name: Cross-Platform Server Support
candidates.description: The reporting system must run on both Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 and Solaris 10 on SPARC hardware so that it operates in the primary and disaster-recovery/reporting server environments.

candidates.name: Non-Disruptive Report Processing
candidates.description: The system must process searches and reports during open hours without disrupting other system functions, including circulation-client operation and patron access to the OPAC. Complex reports must be capable of being queued and processed in the background or otherwise isolated through read-only reporting infrastructure.
candidates.source_priority_note: D16 calls uninterrupted operation during open hours the key requirement

candidates.name: Legacy Browser Support
candidates.description: The system must support Microsoft Internet Explorer 6.0 and later and Firefox 2.0 and later so libraries using these browsers can access the reporting system.

candidates.name: Section 508 Accessibility
candidates.description: The system must comply with Section 508 and support staff using screen readers such as JAWS and NVDA, screen-magnification software such as ZoomText, and other assistive technologies. Its HTML output must be standards-compliant, properly structured, and include alternative text, ARIA labels, and semantic HTML so blind and other disabled staff can run reports.
candidates.source_priority_note: D16 describes this requirement as non-negotiable and legally required

candidates.name: Relational Database Integration
candidates.description: The reporting system must work with the existing PostgreSQL 8.3 relational database structure, support complex joins, and use the main relational database rather than requiring a denormalized reporting schema that can create synchronization issues.

candidates.name: Role-Based Access Control
candidates.description: The system must control permissions through security groups and/or roles that can be assigned to individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups. It must support the access levels Patron, Staff, Local Admin, and Global Admin, and changing a user's permissions must be achievable by changing the user's role assignment. Role administration must be straightforward for administrators.
candidates.source_priority_note: D16 describes role-based access control as essential

candidates.name: Separate Operating Environments
candidates.description: The product must provide separate development, production, and training environments so developers can test new reports without affecting production and new staff can practice running reports without risking operational mistakes.

candidates.name: Configuration Migration
candidates.description: The system must provide export and import functionality to migrate configurations developed in development or training into production, including report templates, permission settings, and other configuration.

candidates.name: OPAC Performance Isolation
candidates.description: The management reporting system must not constrain or slow the OPAC; patrons must retain fast, responsive catalog access even when the reporting system performs a large query.
candidates.source_priority_note: D16 identifies separation of reporting from the OPAC as critical

candidates.name: Searchable Online Help
candidates.description: The system must provide online HTML help for staff that is hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable, and easy to navigate, enabling staff to learn how to run reports without contacting IT for routine assistance.

candidates.name: Analyze Collection Use
candidates.description: The management reporting functionality must enable library managers, administrators, and staff to analyze the library collection and how patrons use it for planning, evaluation, and oversight.

candidates.name: Analyze Branch Capacity
candidates.description: The management reporting functionality must enable library managers, administrators, and staff to analyze branch capacity and determine the optimal distribution of the collection across branches for planning and oversight.

candidates.name: Analyze Patron Demographics
candidates.description: The management reporting functionality must enable library managers, administrators, and staff to analyze patron demographics and interests to support planning and evaluation of library services.

candidates.name: Analyze Staff Productivity
candidates.description: The management reporting functionality must enable library managers, administrators, and staff to analyze staff productivity and workflow for management oversight and service evaluation.

candidates.name: Track Financial Transactions
candidates.description: The management reporting functionality must enable authorized library managers, administrators, and staff to track and verify financial transactions for management oversight.

candidates.name: Provide Report Templates
candidates.description: The product must provide templates needed by all PINES libraries for their management reporting activities.

candidates.name: Consortium Scale Support
candidates.description: The management processes must support a library consortium with 286 locations, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing and processing over 900,000 items per year.
candidates.source_priority_note: D18 describes this capability as highly desirable

candidates.name: Non-Disruptive Report Processing
candidates.description: Searches and reports must be processable during open hours without slowing or disrupting circulation and other system functions, including through background processing or queuing when needed.

candidates.name: Cross-Branch Comparisons
candidates.description: The reporting functionality must provide reports that compare data across library branches or locations for library management.

candidates.name: Report Queue Visibility
candidates.description: Authorized staff must be able to view the status and visibility of reports submitted for processing, so they can determine whether reports are queued, running, completed, or otherwise unavailable.

candidates.name: Predefined Executive Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide predefined reports for board and executive reporting needs.

candidates.name: Data Quality Reports
candidates.description: The reporting functionality must provide reports that identify or communicate data quality problems to staff.

candidates.name: In-Transit Item Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide reports on items currently in transit between locations to support delivery coordination.
candidates.source_priority_note: D18 records in-transit item reports as critical

candidates.name: Branch Missing Damage Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide missing-item and damaged-item reports for individual branches.

candidates.name: Weeding Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide reports to support collection weeding activities.

candidates.name: Shelf Space Utilization
candidates.description: The system must provide reports showing shelf space utilization to support branch and collection management.

candidates.name: Demographic Analysis Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide demographic analysis reports for library program planning.

candidates.name: Linux Solaris Operation
candidates.description: The management processes must operate on a Linux or Solaris server.

candidates.name: Browser Client Access
candidates.description: The management processes must be accessible through a web browser or a Windows-compatible client.
candidates.source_priority_note: D18 calls this critical

candidates.name: Supported Web Browsers
candidates.description: When accessed through a web browser, the management processes must support Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6.0 and later and Mozilla Firefox version 2.0 and later.

candidates.name: Assistive Technology Access
candidates.description: The management processes must be accessible using screen-reading software, screen-magnification software, and other accessibility software, including JAWS, NVDA, and ZoomText, and must satisfy Section 508 accessibility requirements.
candidates.source_priority_note: D18 describes Section 508 compliance as mandatory and identifies accessibility as a legal requirement

candidates.name: Relational Database Backend
candidates.description: The management processes must use a fully relational database back end and work with the relational data structure used for reporting.

candidates.name: Standards-Compliant HTML
candidates.description: The system must produce valid, standards-compliant HTML for report displays, the help system, and web-based user-interface components.

candidates.name: Development Training Environment
candidates.description: The system must provide separate development and training environments in which configurations, including report templates and other report configurations, can be migrated to a production environment through export and import or equivalent migration capability.

candidates.name: Role-Based Access Control
candidates.description: The system must control user rights and privileges through security groups or roles that support access control for individual users, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups.
candidates.source_priority_note: D18 describes this capability as essential

candidates.name: OPAC Function Preservation
candidates.description: Management-process requirements and functionality must not constrain or adversely affect the functionality or features of the Online Public Access Catalog.

candidates.name: Record Data Specifications
candidates.description: The product must provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other records maintained or accessed by the management processes, enabling staff to understand the data structures used for queries.

candidates.name: Process Documentation
candidates.description: The product documentation must provide thorough high-level descriptions of major processes, including bibliographic record import and export, validation of bibliographic records against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.

candidates.name: Online Cross-Linked Help
candidates.description: The system must provide an online, hierarchical, cross-linked HTML help system that describes and illustrates all system functions and is available without requiring staff to leave the system.
candidates.source_priority_note: D18 describes context-sensitive help as critical

candidates.name: Meaningful Error Feedback
candidates.description: The system must provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback when operations or reports fail, and must provide low-level query-specific feedback through the front-end interface to Local and Global System Administrators.

candidates.name: Enterprise ILS Integration
candidates.description: The management processes must use the data structures and functionality of an enterprise-level Library Automation System, including its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, rather than independently managing those functions.

candidates.name: Vendor Data Integration
candidates.description: The management processes must interface with vendor websites through published APIs and/or automated transfers of standard-format data files, including formats such as USMARC21 and EDIFACT, so reporting can use data from external sources.

candidates.name: OPAC Data Access
candidates.description: The management processes must interact with the Online Public Access Catalog and query patron data created there, including holds and circulation data.

candidates.name: Relational Database Backend
candidates.description: The Management Processes reporting system must use a fully relational database backend and operate with the relational data structure rather than relying on denormalization or a separate reporting warehouse synchronized with the live database.

candidates.name: Standards-Compliant HTML
candidates.description: The web interface, help system, and report output must produce HTML that validates against W3C standards to support compatibility with different browsers and assistive technologies.

candidates.name: Environment Configuration Migration
candidates.description: The system must support separate development, training, and production environments and allow administrators to export and import templates, permission settings, and saved queries between those environments.

candidates.name: Safe Training Environment
candidates.description: The training environment must allow staff to experiment without risking production data.

candidates.name: Role-Based Access Control
candidates.description: The system must provide security groups or roles that control access for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups, with permission changes managed by changing role assignments. It must support Global Admin full system access, Local Admin branch-level reporting and configuration, Library Manager execution of approved reports with limited template modification, Staff execution of reports within assigned permissions, and indirect Patron access through OPAC displays.

candidates.name: OPAC Performance Isolation
candidates.description: The management reporting system must remain separate from the public catalog so that running a report does not slow down the OPAC.
candidates.source_priority_note: D19 describes preventing any OPAC constraint as absolute

candidates.name: Complete Data Specifications
candidates.description: The product must provide complete data specifications and data dictionaries for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other records maintained or accessed by Management Processes, including field names, data types, and relationships so staff can write effective queries.

candidates.name: Process Documentation
candidates.description: The product must provide thorough high-level descriptions of major processes, including bibliographic record import and export, validation of bibliographic records against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.

candidates.name: Accessible Online Help
candidates.description: The system must provide an online help system in HTML that is hierarchical, cross-linked, and accessible to users of screen readers.

candidates.name: Detailed Error Reporting
candidates.description: The system must provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback, plus low-level query-specific feedback for administrators. Failed reports must identify relevant details such as the table, field, and type of error rather than only returning a generic failure message.

candidates.name: Centralized Multi-Location Service
candidates.description: Management Processes must be consolidated at a central location that accepts input from and provides services to multiple library locations, supporting a single source of truth for reporting.

candidates.name: Library Automation Integration
candidates.description: Management Processes must rely on and read the data structures and functionality of the enterprise-level Library Automation System, including its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, without managing acquisitions or cataloging data.

candidates.name: Vendor Data Integration
candidates.description: Management Processes must interface with vendor websites through published APIs and/or automated transfers of standard-format data files, including formats such as USMARC21 and EDIFACT, while accommodating libraries where particular vendor data is unavailable.

candidates.name: Read-Only OPAC Data Access
candidates.description: Management Processes must interact with the OPAC patron interface by querying data such as holds and circulation transactions, without modifying that data.

candidates.name: Report Output Formats
candidates.description: The reporting system must produce reports in Excel, HTML, and CSV formats to support web display, business-user pivot-table work, and reliable data export.

candidates.name: Real-Time Historical Reporting
candidates.description: The reporting system must support reports using current real-time data, such as items overdue today, and reports using historical data, such as the bill amount on a specified past date.

candidates.name: Report Cancellation
candidates.description: The system must allow users to cancel scheduled or currently running reports, including while report processing is underway.

candidates.name: Complete Null Results
candidates.description: Reports and data exports must include records containing null values or blank fields rather than excluding those results.

candidates.name: Survey Name Filtering
candidates.description: The reporting system must allow users to filter by survey name and must resolve the supplied survey name to the corresponding survey ID internally.

candidates.name: Retain Transaction History
candidates.description: The system must retain transaction history for a configurable number of days and retain monthly and annual aggregates indefinitely.

candidates.name: Group Transactions By Dimensions
candidates.description: The system must group transaction reports by hour, terminal, branch, and system so staff can identify activity patterns and busy periods.

candidates.name: Count Check-In Methods
candidates.description: The system must count check-ins individually and cumulatively by method, including book drop, terminal, staff user, and self-service.

candidates.name: Count Check-Out Types
candidates.description: The system must count check-outs individually and cumulatively by staff checkout, self checkout, staff renewal, self checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal.

candidates.name: Report Hold Placement Methods
candidates.description: The system must report holds according to their placement method, including staff desk, public computer, and remote placement.

candidates.name: Aggregate Transaction Totals
candidates.description: The system must report holds placed, holds filled, and check-outs per patron, library, group of libraries, system, and county, and must support total transaction counts at the applicable patron, library, and system levels.

candidates.name: Provide Demographic Statistics
candidates.description: The system must provide transaction statistics by geographical region and age range, including useful demographic dimensions such as zip code, while anonymizing the data so that personally identifiable information is not exposed.

candidates.name: Analyze Patron Behavior
candidates.description: The system must produce statistics for understanding and predicting patron behavior and material use, including return speed, renewal rates, the percentage of check-outs that are renewals, and the likelihood that a book will be renewed.

candidates.name: Create Reusable Report Templates
candidates.description: Administrators must be able to create report templates and run them as-is or modify them before execution.

candidates.name: Control Report Permissions
candidates.description: The system must provide fine-grained permissions controlling who can create, run, and clone particular reports.

candidates.name: Control Shared Report Access
candidates.description: The system must provide shared folders that allow or disallow staff from running specific reports.

candidates.name: Show Report Queue Position
candidates.description: The system must show a user where their report is in the processing queue and whether it is still being processed.

candidates.name: Save And Reuse Queries
candidates.description: Users must be able to save queries and reuse them for repeated reporting tasks.

candidates.name: Export Multiple Report Formats
candidates.description: The system must provide report output in Excel, CSV, HTML, and pivot-table formats.

candidates.name: Deliver Reports By Email
candidates.description: The system must be able to deliver completed reports by email.

candidates.name: Schedule Recurring Reports
candidates.description: Users must be able to schedule reports to run repeatedly on a recurring basis.

candidates.name: Cancel Report Execution
candidates.description: Users must be able to cancel a scheduled report or a report that is currently running.

candidates.name: Provide Historical Reporting
candidates.description: The system must show what data looked like on a specified date in the past, including historical shelving-location information even when the current shelving location has changed, and must support snapshot bills reporting for past dates.

candidates.name: Provide Real-Time Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide real-time reporting for monitoring busy periods.

candidates.name: Include Empty Report Values
candidates.description: Report results must include null and blank field values rather than omitting records or fields containing them.

candidates.name: Prevent Duplicate Export Rows
candidates.description: Report exports, including Excel exports, must avoid unintended duplicate rows so that the exported data can be used without repeated records.

candidates.name: Select MARC Fields Across Rows
candidates.description: The system must allow reports to retrieve specific MARC fields even when those fields are stored across multiple rows.

candidates.name: Query Candidate Materials
candidates.description: The system must allow users to query for materials that are candidates for administrative actions such as collection review or related material processing.

candidates.name: Select Query Results Manually
candidates.description: Users must be able to manually select individual records from query results for subsequent administrative processing.

candidates.name: Move Items Between Locations
candidates.description: The system must allow authorized users to change item records to move items to a new location.

candidates.name: Revert Item Locations
candidates.description: The system must allow authorized users to revert items to their original locations.

candidates.name: Track Record Deletions
candidates.description: The system must count and track record deletions.

candidates.name: Show Last Item Circulation
candidates.description: Item reports must be able to indicate the last circulation date for each item.

candidates.name: Exclude Renewals From Check-In
candidates.description: Check-in date and time reporting must exclude renewal transactions so that renewal activity is not counted as check-in activity.

requirements.name: Current Last-Copy Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide reports identifying Items that are the only copy within a selected scope, including an individual Branch and the entire Consortium.
requirements.priority_justification: D06 and D15 explicitly call the last-copy report critical, and staff across the consortium depend on identifying the sole remaining copy at branch and consortium scopes.
requirements.source_priority_note: D06 marks the last-copy report critical; D15 calls it critical

requirements.name: Administer Report Permissions
requirements.description: The system must provide fine-grained, role-administered permissions controlling who may create, clone, run, and access reports. Administrators must be able to create shared folders that allow or disallow access to specific reports and ad hoc reports on specified data sets.
requirements.priority_justification: Fine-grained report permissions protect sensitive datasets across multiple sources and complement the system's stated role-based access controls.

requirements.name: Assistive Technology Access
requirements.description: The system must support screen readers, screen-magnification software, and other assistive technologies, including JAWS, NVDA, and ZoomText, and comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks assistive technology support High Priority, while D16 calls accessibility non-negotiable and D18 describes Section 508 compliance as mandatory.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority; D16 calls accessibility non-negotiable and D18 calls Section 508 compliance mandatory

requirements.name: Consortium Scale Support
requirements.description: The system must support a library consortium with 286 locations, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing or processing more than 900,000 items per year.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks consortium-scale support High Priority, and the specified locations, circulation, and processing volumes define the system's operating context.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

requirements.name: Financial Audit Compliance
requirements.description: The system's reports and archived data must comply with standard accounting practice and applicable state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.
requirements.priority_justification: The requirement explicitly calls for compliance with applicable state, county, and municipal auditing requirements, so financial reporting must meet those obligations.

requirements.name: Item Status Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide periodic management reports identifying items that have not been checked out for a specified number of days, items with item-level holds, in-transit items with outstanding holds, last copies, and missing items.
requirements.priority_justification: The fixed Last Copy Reports requirement depends on identifying last copies, and the requested item-status reports also cover missing and in-transit items used in collection management.

requirements.name: Multi-Record Query Interface
requirements.description: The system must provide a user-friendly query-design interface for bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, and financial records. Users must be able to select fields, choose values from picklists, select regular expressions from a dropdown, and use Boolean operators.
requirements.priority_justification: D10, D12, and D18 request querying across major record types, and without a flexible query interface users would be unable to build many of the system’s core reports.

requirements.name: Non-Disruptive Report Processing
requirements.description: The system must process searches and reports during open hours without disrupting other system functions, including circulation and patron access to the OPAC. Long-running reports must be capable of background processing or other isolation from operational activity.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks open-hours report processing High Priority, and D14, D16, and D18 also address avoiding disruption to live services.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks the open-hours operating requirement High Priority

requirements.name: Online System Help
requirements.description: The system must provide online HTML help that is hierarchical, cross-linked, and describes and illustrates system functions. Staff must be able to find help without leaving the system, and the help must be accessible to screen-reader users.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks online system help High Priority, and the requirement is repeated across five sources, including accessibility for screen-reader users.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

requirements.name: Payment Audit Ledger
requirements.description: The system must maintain a ledger of patron payments identifying the specific charges to which each payment was applied, so finance staff can trace payments and reconcile accounts.
requirements.priority_justification: D11 calls the financial audit trail critical, and finance staff need payment-to-charge detail to trace and reconcile accounts.
requirements.source_priority_note: D11 calls the financial audit trail critical

requirements.name: Preserve OPAC Functionality
requirements.description: Management reporting functionality must not constrain or adversely affect the functionality or performance of the Online Public Access Catalog.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks OPAC preservation High Priority, and D16 calls separation from OPAC functionality critical because reporting must not impair patron access.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority; D16 calls OPAC separation critical

requirements.name: Privacy-Protecting Transaction Archives
requirements.description: The system must archive transaction data for the period required by applicable law while protecting patron privacy by removing personally identifiable information and retaining useful demographic statistics.
requirements.priority_justification: D12 states that State law requires transaction retention and privacy protection, making the archive behavior a compliance obligation.
requirements.source_priority_note: D12 states that State law requires this transaction retention and privacy protection for compliance

requirements.name: Record Data Specifications
requirements.description: Product documentation must provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other records maintained or accessed by the Management Processes, including field names, data types, and relationships.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks complete record data specifications High Priority, and these details support administration and interpretation across the system's record types.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

requirements.name: Relational Database Support
requirements.description: The system must use and work with a fully relational database structure and support reporting queries across relational data. It must not require a denormalized reporting schema synchronized with the live database.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks relational database support High Priority, and the requirement is repeated across four sources for reporting against relational data.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks the relational database requirement High Priority

requirements.name: Role-Based Access Control
requirements.description: The system must control user rights through security groups or roles assigned to individuals, workgroups, and staff groups, and allow administrators to manage permissions through role assignment. Roles must support access appropriate to staff, managers, local administrators, and global administrators.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks role-based access High Priority, and the requirement is repeated in several sources for controlling staff and administrator permissions.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

requirements.name: Server Operating Environment
requirements.description: The system must operate on Linux or Solaris servers, including the Linux and Solaris environments used for production and disaster recovery.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks Linux or Solaris operation High Priority, and D16 and D18 also specify those server environments.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

requirements.name: Standards-Compliant HTML
requirements.description: The system must produce standards-compliant HTML for web interfaces, help content, and report output.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks standards-compliant HTML High Priority, with three other sources also specifying the output requirement.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

requirements.name: Transit Location Reports
requirements.description: The system must report items in transit by sending library and destination library, and provide reports of items currently in transit between locations for delivery coordination.
requirements.priority_justification: D18 explicitly records in-transit item reports as critical, and delivery coordination depends on knowing sending and destination locations.
requirements.source_priority_note: D18 records in-transit item reports as critical

requirements.name: Enforce Archive Retention
requirements.description: The system must enforce data-archiving retention policies required for audits, including a seven-year retention period where applicable under state and local requirements.
requirements.priority_justification: The requirement specifies retention periods required for audits, including seven years where state and local rules apply, making enforcement a compliance obligation.

requirements.name: Read-Only OPAC Data Access
requirements.description: Management Processes must interact with the OPAC patron interface by querying data such as holds and circulation transactions, without modifying that data.
requirements.priority_justification: Read-only OPAC access protects patron-facing holds and circulation data from management-process changes, aligning with the multi-source requirement to preserve OPAC functionality.

requirements.name: Material Volume Reporting
requirements.description: The system must report material volume for a specified library at the current time or a selected historical point, separating new acquisitions, items on the shelf, items in circulation, and totals. Users must be able to break results down by categories such as total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books, customize categories, and report volume added in periods such as the last 30, 60, or 90 days.
requirements.priority_justification: The reports support collection planning, but the system can provide its broader reporting workflows without every requested volume breakdown.
requirements.source_priority_note: D01 calls this a key requirement

requirements.name: Branch Capacity Interface
requirements.description: The system must provide authorized users, including branch managers, with an overview of capacity across all Branches using a defined capacity measure, with the ability to drill into individual Branches, sort and filter by region, library type, and current load, view growth or shrinkage trends, and export the information to CSV.
requirements.priority_justification: D02, D10, and D17 support a branch-capacity overview that helps authorized staff compare locations, though reporting can operate without this specialized view.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Usage Report
requirements.description: The system must compare, for each material genre and format, the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection, and the percentage of total shelf space. Results must be available per library and system-wide, support date-range comparisons, and provide a side-by-side library comparison view. When shelf-space measurements are unavailable, the system must estimate shelf space using available item dimensions or item count as a proxy.
requirements.priority_justification: The comparisons help libraries make collection and shelf-space decisions, but they are a specialized analysis rather than a prerequisite for core reporting.

requirements.name: Generate Transfer Pull Lists
requirements.description: The system must generate printable pull lists identifying items selected for transfer so staff can retrieve them for movement.
requirements.priority_justification: Printable pull lists help staff retrieve selected items accurately, while transfers can still be coordinated through other procedures.

requirements.name: Preview Pending Transfers
requirements.description: Before applying a transfer, the system must show a preview of the proposed changes, including the number of items and their source and destination locations, and require confirmation before making the changes.
requirements.priority_justification: A preview and confirmation reduce accidental transfer changes, but they support rather than enable the system's broader workflows.

requirements.name: Query and Select Transfer Candidates
requirements.description: The system must allow authorized staff to query candidate materials for transfer or other administrative processing using conditions such as material type, section, genre, or circulation history, and to manually select individual titles or items, including only part of a larger candidate set, for subsequent processing.
requirements.priority_justification: D04, D15, and D20 request selecting transfer candidates, which makes transfer workflows more targeted but is not needed for reporting or other core functions.

requirements.name: Restrict Transfer Permissions
requirements.description: The system must restrict item transfers to authorized roles, including managers, administrators, or transfer coordinators, and prevent unauthorized staff from performing transfers.
requirements.priority_justification: Role restrictions reduce the risk of unauthorized transfers, although this control applies to a narrower workflow than the system's general access management.

requirements.name: Revert Transferred Items
requirements.description: The system must automatically or manually return transferred Items to their original Branches after a configured period or when configured criteria are met, including time-based conditions and Item-status or destination events.
requirements.priority_justification: D04, D10, D15, and D20 request reversion to manage temporary transfers, but transfers can still be handled without automatic or criteria-based returns.
requirements.source_priority_note: D04 calls automatic reversion important

requirements.name: Save Reusable Queries
requirements.description: The system must allow users to save queries for repeated use, including recurring transfer and reporting tasks.
requirements.priority_justification: Reusable queries reduce repeated setup for recurring tasks, although users can still run those tasks by recreating queries.
requirements.source_priority_note: D04 calls saving queries for repeated use crucial

requirements.name: Transfer History Records
requirements.description: The system must retain transfer activity for audit and expose item transfer history so staff can review completed and reverted transfers and determine how often an item has moved.
requirements.priority_justification: Transfer history helps staff audit movements and answer item-history questions, but it is specific to the transfer utility.

requirements.name: Transfer Item Batches
requirements.description: The system must provide authorized staff with a utility to transfer batches of selected Items between Branches or other locations, including mobile libraries, outreach collections, warehouses, book sales, and event locations, and to update the selected Items’ location records to the transfer destination.
requirements.priority_justification: Staff need batch transfers to update item locations across the varied branches and other locations described in the sources, though other reporting and library operations can function without this utility.

requirements.name: Delayed Transit Items Report
requirements.description: The system must generate one report of items that have remained in transit longer than a configurable number of days, with views per branch and system-wide. The report must combine transit-to and transit-from items, identify items with no arrival date and an overdue departure date, and allow sorting by due date. Seven days is suggested as the default threshold.
requirements.priority_justification: The report helps staff investigate overdue transit items, while the broader system can operate without this particular exception report.

requirements.name: Missing Damaged Items Report
requirements.description: The system must provide a report of missing and damaged items by branch. The report must include item condition notes and support date ranges for trend analysis.
requirements.priority_justification: Branch-level missing and damaged-item trends inform collection oversight, but this specialized report is not needed for other reporting workflows.

requirements.name: Audit Record Deletions
requirements.description: The system must retain an audit record of successful deletions, including record type, record identifier, timestamp, user, and user location. This tracking must cover purge activity and other record deletions.
requirements.priority_justification: Deletion audit records help administrators investigate changes across several source documents, but the system's reporting workflows can run without the audit feature.

requirements.name: Confirm Purge Deletions
requirements.description: The system must require a separate confirmation step before executing purge deletions, distinct from identifying and reviewing candidates.
requirements.priority_justification: A separate confirmation step helps prevent accidental purge deletions, but it supports rather than enables candidate identification and review.

requirements.name: Delete Itemless Records
requirements.description: The system must provide a method to delete records that have no items attached during collection cleanup.
requirements.priority_justification: Removing itemless records helps keep the catalog clean, although users can operate the reporting system without this cleanup method.

requirements.name: Delete Volumes With Copies
requirements.description: The system must provide a method to delete volume entries together with their associated copy entries during collection cleanup.
requirements.priority_justification: Deleting volumes with associated copies supports collection cleanup, but it is a specialized maintenance operation rather than a general reporting dependency.

requirements.name: Deleted Last-Copy Reports
